title: per-request-workload-mapping-token-cost-matrix-hosted-api
linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE-1234: Hosted API unit econ baseline
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working worksheet maps representative request types (by traffic surface) to per-token COGS and margin pathways across regions and model variants. Goal is to produce a compact per-request matrix that product and sales teams can use to estimate incremental cost and suggested levers (batching, q-profile, routing) for observed traffic mixes. Draft for internal review — contains rough samples and conservative assumptions.

Versioning and notes:
- v0.1 created 2025-11-02 by Samir (initial mapping of traffic segments)
- v0.2 2026-01-15 added regional GPU rate adjustments and quantization profiles (Aisha)
- v0.3 2026-02-28 incorporated recent throughput numbers from serving-runtime perf run (Renee)
- This sheet is intentionally compact: separate detailed models live in /optimize/token-cost-simulators.

Methodology (short):
1) Collect sample request archetypes from 3 customers + platform telemetry (common surfaces): chat-short, chat-long, summarization-batch, classification, embeddings-batch, rerank.
2) For each archetype define: input tokens median, output tokens median, typical temperature/beam, model family (e.g., open-7b, redwood-13b, redwood-XXL), expected sequence distribution.
3) Map to a serving configuration: GPU class (A100-80GB, H100-80GB), quantization profile (fp16, q4_0, q4_1), batching policy (real-time low-latency vs throughput-batched), and cache hit rate assumptions.
4) Use measured tokens/s and regional instance rates to compute marginal COGS per 1k tokens and per-request incremental cost.

Legend for table columns (sheet view):
- TrafficSegment: short label for archetype
- ExampleUse: 1–2 sentence example
- MedianInputTokens / MedianOutputTokens
- ModelVariant: family + size
- QProfile: fp16 | q4_0 | q4_1 | q8_0
- GPUClass: A100 | H100 | T4 (for embeddings)
- SeqP50: median seq length used for kernel selection
- TokensPerSecond: observed tokens/s (end-to-end serving, with batching off/on where applicable)
- InstanceCostPerHourUSD: region-specific GPU-hour 
- EffectiveCostPer1kTokensUSD: computed marginal cost per 1k tokens (includes infra + amortized model memory egress + minimal infra overhead 5%)
- SuggestedLevers: concise list (batch window, QProfile change, route-to-dedicated, cache)

Sample rows (conservative numbers; used formulas in separate tab):
1) TrafficSegment: chat_short_low 
   ExampleUse: 1–3 turn conversational assistant, avg 80i / 40o tokens
   ModelVariant: open-7b (fp16)
   GPUClass: A100-80GB
   SeqP50: 120
   TokensPerSecond: 1500
   InstanceCostPerHourUSD (us-west1): 4.8
   EffectiveCostPer1kTokensUSD: $0.0065
   SuggestedLevers: enable prefix cache (expected 15% token saving), route to q4_1 where latency OK

2) TrafficSegment: chat_long_codegen 
   ExampleUse: multi-turn developer assistant producing 400 tokens output
   ModelVariant: redwood-13b (q4_0)
   GPUClass: H100-80GB
   SeqP50: 600
   TokensPerSecond: 900
   InstanceCostPerHourUSD (eu-central1): 9.6
   EffectiveCostPer1kTokensUSD: $0.022
   SuggestedLevers: higher batching window during background traffic, early-stop heuristics for code generation, fallback smaller model for inference-only calls

3) TrafficSegment: embeddings_batch_64
   ExampleUse: semantic search indexing, 64 embeddings per request
   ModelVariant: embeddings-large (fp16)
   GPUClass: T4
   SeqP50: 64
   TokensPerSecond: 250000 (vector-only throughput)
   InstanceCostPerHourUSD (us-east1): 1.2
   EffectiveCostPer1kTokensUSD: $0.0008
   SuggestedLevers: keep on shared low-cost fleet, aggressive packing to exploit batch-size amplification

Key observations from early runs:
- Quantization moves (fp16 -> q4_0/q4_1) show 1.6x–2.4x token-cost improvements for medium/long sequence workloads with small model-quality delta in our internal evals. For chat_short the margin is smaller.
- Batching benefits are highly traffic-shape dependent: sub-100ms P95 latency targets limit batch windows; background indexing/embedding workloads can use 200–400ms windows yielding 2–3x cost reductions.
- Regional GPU-hour variance (H100 vs A100 pricing) dominates small model deltas for high-token workloads: route affinity by model-size + region gives 8–15% COGS swing.
- Prefix/KV cache effectiveness depends on prompt homogeneity. For assistant-style calls we measured 10–25% token saving on high-repeat sessions.

Recommended actionables (prioritized):
1) Build a per-route token-cost API (internal) that returns estimated COGS for a given request sample (payload size, model preference, latency SLO). This will standardize pricing/alerts for hosted customers. Owner: Diego. ETA: 6 weeks.
2) Pilot region-aware routing policy for high-volume customers: route long-sequence/throughput workloads to lower-cost regions automatically with optional customer opt-out. Owner: Product + Infra. ETA: 8–10 weeks.
3) Expand q-profiles in model catalog with explicit quality/latency tags; expose recommended q-profile per archetype in Console. Owner: Applied ML. ETA: 4 weeks (mvp).
4) Draft customer-facing one-pager showing per-traffic-segment savings levers (batching, q-profile, routing). Sales to use in renewal playbook. Owner: Growth. ETA: 3 weeks.

Sensitivity notes and downside risks:
- Model quality regressions: q-profile savings are not uniform; need evaluation harness against customers' reference prompts before defaulting to lower precision. Linked to CONFLUENCE-1234.
- Latency SLO violations: aggressive batching can increase P95 dramatically. Must pair with SRE SLO guardrails.
- Accounting complexity: per-request COGS API will require telemetry alignment and proper attribution to avoid billing disputes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Define canonical traffic-segment taxonomy (who owns this?) Suggest product-optimize + solutions-engineering co-own.
- [ ] Add cold-start impact to instance-cost calculations (current model assumes steady-state).
- [ ] Determine how to show recommended lever next to per-route metrics in Console (UI designs needed).
- [ ] Run AB test on routing long-sequence to eu vs us for one mid-market customer (Renee to coordinate).

Appendix: simple formula references used in sheet:
- EffectiveCostPer1kTokens = (InstanceCostPerHourUSD / (TokensPerSecond * 3600) * 1000) * (1 + infra_overhead_pct) - token_savings_from_cache
- Instance-hours required per million tokens = (1_000_000 / (TokensPerSecond * 3600))
- SavingsPct from batching ~ min(1, batch_amplification_factor * observed_batch_fill) - measured empirically per model

Last section: quick example pricing callout (for conversation) 
- For typical chat_short volume of 10M tokens/month on open-7b fp16 in us-west1: baseline COGS ~ $65/month. If we enable q4_1 + 15% prefix cache + mild batching (50ms window) we estimate COGS drops to $28–32/month (~50%+ saving).
- For large codegen workloads (redwood-13b q4_0) 10M tokens/month baseline ~ $220–260; with batching + routing to eu we see 20–40% reductions depending on latency constraint.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally high-level and contains conservative estimates. Please flag any model family or regional pricing updates; I will re-run the detailed simulator and update v0.4.

End of sheet.
